decisions.executionNote: Begin elevated, elbow-continuous approach; rotate both open grippers toward a top grasp. Estimate block geometry from head RGB; plan a central blue base.
The first approach was rejected without motion; restart with much smaller translation and rotation increments to preserve joint continuity.
Continue gradually raising and advancing the open grippers while pitching down, with arms on their respective sides.
Advance above the red and blue blocks while continuing the gradual downward tool rotation; remain elevated for clearance.
Bring both wrists above their blocks at clearance height, continuing the elbow-up top-grasp orientation without crossing.
Replan from the single executed step, reducing forward travel and pitch increments after the continuity guard. Keep clearance above the blocks.
Complete most of the downward pitch while centering above red with the left arm and blue with the right. Both grippers remain open.
Use reduced increments after the guard to align vertically over red and blue, then inspect grasp height before closing.
Lower the nearly vertical, open grippers in small increments, checking fingertip clearance and centering against RGB before grasping.
Refine fore-aft alignment from the wrist views and descend slowly around red and blue; open jaws approach the block side faces.
Vertical tracking suggests the open fingertips reached the table; stop descending, ease up slightly, and close around the red and blue blocks. Retention must be checked by lifting.
Lift both blocks with closed grippers to verify retention; move red slightly left for clearance while preparing to put blue at the center boundary.
RGB shows both blocks retained. Shift blue to the workspace boundary as the base while keeping red elevated and safely to the left.
Keep red clear at its observed pose; lower retained blue slowly to the table at the center, avoiding further inward arm motion.
Set blue onto the table and open the right gripper, then rise vertically to leave the bottom block undisturbed. Red remains held on the left.
Blue is released on the table. Move the empty right arm outward toward cyan while carrying red toward the central base, maintaining separation and elevation.
Raise and separate the right gripper farther from blue before proceeding to cyan. Carry red above the base slowly; blue may have shifted slightly during clearance.
Move the right arm well outward above cyan to relieve possible close-arm interference. Keep red held above the central stack area; reassess the shifted blue base.
Bring retained red toward the observed blue base near the center; lower the right gripper above cyan and gently restore its vertical orientation.
Visually align red above the settled blue base and lower toward stacking height. Center the open right gripper around cyan with a slow approach.
Seat red gently on blue with a small lateral correction. Close the right gripper around cyan at the established grasp height, then pause before release/lift checks.
Open the left gripper fully and wait without lateral motion to release red on blue. Lift cyan vertically with the right gripper closed to verify retention.
Withdraw the open left gripper straight upward to protect the red-on-blue stack. Raise retained cyan to clear the two-block stack before lateral transfer.
The upward withdrawal hit a continuity guard after two steps. Replan with smaller upward and outward left-arm motion, easing pitch while keeping the jaws open; continue raising cyan.
Red remains over blue after release. Retract the empty left arm to its own side while transporting retained cyan above the stack at clearance height.
No motion occurred on rejection. Halve the left retreat and pitch increments for continuity while moving cyan toward the stack with the right arm.
Continue retracting the open left arm. Bring cyan over the visually stable red-on-blue stack, staying high until alignment can be checked.
Center cyan over red and descend conservatively toward the third-layer height. Continue the left arm's outward return without disturbing the stack.
Lower cyan the last few millimeters toward contact on red, then pause with a closed grip. Continue returning the empty left arm along a smooth outward path.
Release cyan with a stationary open right gripper and allow the stack to settle. Smoothly continue the left arm's return toward its initial pose.
Withdraw the fully open right gripper vertically from cyan without dragging the stack; approach the left origin smoothly with decreasing translation.
The three colors remain vertically stacked after release. Retract the right arm outward and back while easing its pitch; finish the left return with small increments.
The previous retreat was rejected before motion. Reduce right-arm translation and pitch increments to preserve continuity while keeping both grippers open.
Complete the left origin alignment with tiny increments. Continue the right arm's elevated, elbow-up return away from the untouched stack.
The stack appears to have shifted during retreat. Stop sideways rotation and raise the open right gripper vertically for safer clearance, then reassess stability.
The stack toppled; rebuild with the right arm while the left stays reset. Reorient vertically above the separated blocks, allowing them to settle before the next grasp.
Approach red from above and turn the open right gripper so the jaws can close fore-aft, avoiding the neighboring blocks on either side.
Continue the gradual yaw change at clearance height, aligning the right wrist above red for a fore-aft grasp; left remains reset.
Finish rotating the right gripper to a fore-aft grasp and lower above red slowly; neighboring blue and cyan remain on the table.
Lower the fore-aft-oriented open jaws around red in small vertical steps, watching clearance to the adjacent blocks.
Descend the last twelve millimeters to the established table grasp height, then close on red without lateral movement. Check retention before stacking again.
Finish closing on red, then lift straight up for a visual retention check. Keep the left arm at rest and avoid sweeping the neighboring blocks.
Red is visibly retained. Lift it above blue's top before transferring leftward toward the base, keeping the vertical fore-aft grasp and leaving the reset left arm stationary.
Align retained red directly over the blue base using the latest head and wrist views. Keep generous vertical clearance during the small lateral correction, then start a cautious descent.
Lower retained red toward blue with a tiny centering correction. Keep the fore-aft grasp vertical, and stop near contact before opening.
Seat red gently on blue, then open the right gripper without translating or rotating. Allow the two-block stack to settle before a strictly vertical withdrawal.
Withdraw the open right gripper straight upward, maintaining orientation and horizontal position until the fingertips fully clear red. Leave the left arm reset.
The released red remains on blue. Gain additional vertical clearance, then move the open right gripper toward cyan without rotating or sweeping through the stack.
Center the open right gripper over cyan and descend vertically away from the stable red-on-blue stack. Keep the left arm reset and inspect final grasp alignment before closing.
Lower the open right gripper toward cyan with a small fore-aft centering correction. Preserve the vertical orientation and keep clear of the red-on-blue stack.
Descend the final twelve millimeters around cyan, then close without lateral motion. Keep the two-block stack undisturbed and verify retention by a subsequent vertical lift.
Finish closing around cyan, then lift vertically to check retention. Keep the right wrist orientation fixed and leave the existing red-on-blue stack untouched.
Cyan remains visibly retained. Raise it vertically above the two-block stack before translating, maintaining the closed grip and fixed wrist orientation.
Carry retained cyan above the red-on-blue stack at clearance height. Keep the vertical wrist orientation fixed and inspect centering before descending.
Cyan appears offset right of red in the head view. Correct leftward at clearance height while lowering only slightly; keep the grasp closed and orientation fixed.
Cyan is visually centered over red. Descend vertically in small increments toward third-layer contact, keeping the closed grip and fixed orientation.
Seat cyan the last few millimeters on red, then open without translating or rotating. Allow the three blocks to settle before withdrawing strictly upward.
Withdraw the fully open right gripper straight upward from cyan, keeping orientation and horizontal position fixed to avoid disturbing the rebuilt stack.
Gain additional straight-up fingertip clearance before any lateral return. Keep both grippers open and the right wrist orientation fixed to protect the stack.
The stack remains standing after vertical clearance. Move the open right gripper outward at fixed height and orientation before rotating; correct the left arm's small origin drift.
The three-block stack remains standing. Continue moving the empty right arm outward with clearance, gradually unwinding its yaw toward the initial orientation; both grippers stay open.
Continue the right arm's reset away from the stable stack, gradually unwinding yaw with small outward and backward movements. Both grippers remain open.
Continue resetting the right arm well clear of the standing stack, gradually restoring the initial orientation and moving backward with both grippers open.
The blue-red-cyan stack remains standing. Continue a smooth right-arm return toward its initial pose with open grippers, correcting only tiny left-arm drift.
Continue the right arm's gradual return toward its initial position and orientation, maintaining joint continuity and leaving the standing stack untouched.

The blue-red-cyan stack remains standing. Continue the right arm's smooth reset with decreasing translation, while correcting tiny left-origin drift and keeping both grippers open.
